messages.subject: Re: master thesis: performing asymmetric VECM
messages.body_plain:
Dear Simon

Yes package tsDyn can help you for this. See the function TVECM, that normally estimates the thresholds parameter, but you can for sure also impose its value to be 0. Usually, the cointegrating will be also searched fr, but you can also impose its value to correspond to the value estimated in the linear VECM (either Engle-Granger 2 step or Johansen ML). See code below.

Kindly let us know once your thesis is written, we always appreciate to have feedback on what is done with tsDyn!

Best

Matthieu

PS: ccing to the package mailing list.

library(tsDyn)

data(zeroyld)
dat<-zeroyld

lin<-VECM(dat,  lag=2)
summary(lin)

lin_johansen<-VECM(dat,  lag=2, estim="ML")
summary(lin_johansen)

##Estimate a TVECM with th imposed
tv<-TVECM(dat, nthresh=1,th1=list(exact=0), lag=2)

##Estimate a TVECM with th and beta imposed
tv<-TVECM(dat, nthresh=1,th1=list(exact=0), lag=2, beta=list(exact=-lin_johansen$model.specific$beta[2,1]))

2012/8/23 Simon Kofoed-Dam <s...@dsr.life.ku.dk>
> Dear Matthieu Stigler
>
> i am studying agricultural economics at the university of Copenhagen, and i am currently working on my master thesis. The subject is price transmission; i have got acces to a big scanner data set on dairy products in Germany. i am looking into relating the retail level prices to the wholesale price (weekly, covering a period of 6 years).
>
> i am looking into how to perform an asymmetric VECM (hence splitting the residuals from the long run equation up into positive and negative values).
>
> I am working in R, and I have been looking a bit on the package tsDyn, where i can see you are the maintainer of the package (and i found this email adress on the R-website). I hope it is okay to write to you about this inquiry.
>
> in tsDyn there is an option of performing an symmetric VECM, hence where the residuals from the LR equation is NOT split up.
>
> I am able to "manually" perform an asymmetric VECM via the Angle-Granger two step procedure. but do you know, if it is possible to perform an asymmetric VECM within the framework of the tsDyn (or a similar package) - especially because i think it would be nice to utilize the Johansen Procedure. and i do not know how to program this procedure "manually".
>
> Do you have a few hints or input on how to perform an Asymmetric VECM?
>
> Kind regards, from Simon Kofoed-Dam
>
>
>

messages.subject: Re: master thesis: performing asymmetric VECM
messages.body_plain:
this is doable through the argument "common", (maybe slightly misleadingly called common), so you want:

common="only_ECT"

Note however that as for now, the ECT term contains only the variable, and no intercept (not available in literature actually) so this might be a problem for your case where arguably the intercept in important in the Long-run relationship.

Best

PS: again ccing to the tsDyn mailing list, so that others might benefit from your question

2012/8/24 Simon Kofoed-Dam <s...@dsr.life.ku.dk>
> Dear Matthieu
>
> thank you very much for the quick and positive response, including the code. Any hints are greatly appreciated. However i am looking into a VECM the error correction term is split up into negative and positive values (otherwise zero) in the same set of equation. not rtwo seperate VECM, based on the threshold for 0. For instance when i implemented the Engle-granger 2 step approach:
>
> step 1/long run equation:
>    P_retail = const. + b1*P_wholesale + e
>
> then splitting the residual into negative and positive (otherwise 0):
>    e_neg <- min(0,e)
>    e_pos <- max(0,e)
>
> finally calculating the step 2 (the actial VECM), (i actually do this by
> utilizing the VAR function in R):
>
>   (2) diff(P_retail)_t = const. + v1*diff(P_retail)_(t-1)
>                                 + v2*diff(P_wholesale)_(t-1)
>                                 + v3*e_neg_(t-1)
>                                 + v4*e_pos_(t-1)
>                                 + error
>
>   (3) diff(P_wholesale)_t = const. + w1*diff(P_retail)_(t-1)
>                                    + w2*diff(P_wholesale)_(t-1)
>                                    + w3*e_neg_(t-1)
>                                    + w4*e_pos_(t-1)
>                                    + error
>
> for the lagged endogenous variables (diff(P_retail)_(t-1) and diff(P_retail)_(t-1)) several lags can be included, according to how the model performs.
>
> below is a sample of the code i have been writing so far - note i am utilizing features in the package "vars". also i am basing my selection of lags on the AIC
>
> (time dimension: 312 weeks of data)
>
> in my code, x is the wholesale price, y is the retail price.
>
> "
> library(vars)
>
> x <- rnorm(312, mean=0, sd=1)
> y <- rnorm(312, mean=0, sd=1)
>
> step1 <- lm(y ~ x)
> res.step1 <- residuals(step1)
>
> #split residuals up into negative and positive
> for (j in 1:length(data.wide.raw[,1])) {res.step1_pos[j] <- max(0,res.step1[j])}
> res.step1_pos.311 <- res.step1_pos[1:311] #for later use in VECM
>
> for (j in 1:length(data.wide.raw[,1])) {res.step1_neg[j] <- min(0,res.step1[j])}
> res.step1_neg.311 <- res.step1_neg[1:311] #for later use in VECM
>
> data.endog <- data.frame(diff(x),diff(y))
> data.ect <- data.frame(res.step1_pos.311, res.step1_neg.311)
>
> #choose optimal lag length using AIC:
> lag_vecm <- VARselect(data.endog, type="const", exogen=data.ect, lag.max=15)$selection[1]
>
> #calculate VECM (in a VAR setup)
> vecm.est <- VAR(data.endog, type="const", exogen=data.ect, p=lag_vecm)
>
> Best regards, from Simon
>
>
